topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(3), is failing to account for and remit money coming into a licensee's possession that belongs to others treated as its own, separate unfair trade practice, distinct from the commingling prohibition?
choice_a: No -- failing to account for and remit money is only ever prosecuted as commingling, never as its own separate ground
choice_b: Yes -- § 43-40-25(b)(3) separately enumerates failing to account for and remit money belonging to others as its own unfair trade practice, apart from the commingling prohibition in § 43-40-25(b)(4)
choice_c: No -- Georgia law only regulates trust fund handling through GAC rule, not through the unfair-trade-practice statute at all
choice_d: Yes, but only if the amount withheld exceeds $10,000
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(3) separately enumerates failing to account for and remit money belonging to others as its own unfair trade practice ground, distinct from -- though related to -- the commingling prohibition in § 43-40-25(b)(4).

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(18), what two things must every written listing agreement include to comply with Georgia license law?
choice_a: The listing broker's Social Security number and the property's tax parcel ID
choice_b: A notarized signature and a witness signature
choice_c: A fixed date of expiration, and a copy left with the party who signed it
choice_d: A minimum commission rate and a maximum commission rate
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(18) makes it an unfair trade practice to fail to include a fixed date of expiration in any written listing agreement, and to fail to leave a copy of it with the signing party.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: A buyer signs a purchase offer, but the licensee waits three weeks before providing the buyer a completed copy of it. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(19), what concern does this raise?
choice_a: No concern -- there is no deadline for delivering a signed offer's copy to the parties
choice_b: A concern only if the offer was ultimately rejected
choice_c: A concern only for listing agreements, not purchase offers
choice_d: Failing to deliver a completed copy of a purchase agreement or offer within a reasonable time is an enumerated unfair trade practice
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(19) makes it an unfair trade practice to fail to deliver, within a reasonable time, a completed copy of any purchase agreement or offer to buy or sell real estate to the party who signed it.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: A disgruntled licensee, after losing a listing to a competitor, files a document purporting to create a lien based on an old, expired listing contract, solely to make the property harder for the new listing agent to sell. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(24), what has this licensee done?
choice_a: Filed a listing contract or lien-purporting document for the purpose of casting a cloud upon title -- an enumerated unfair trade practice
choice_b: Nothing improper, since filing any document with the county is a matter of public record and outside GREC's authority
choice_c: Committed a violation only if the document is later ruled invalid by a court
choice_d: Committed a violation only if the licensee personally profited from the filing
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(24) makes it an unfair trade practice to file a listing contract or any document purporting to create a lien based on a listing contract for the purpose of casting a cloud upon title -- regardless of whether the filing is later invalidated or whether the licensee personally profited.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(25), what general disciplinary ground allows GREC to act against a licensee whose conduct falls short of protecting the public, even without a more specific enumerated violation applying?
choice_a: GREC has no catch-all disciplinary authority beyond the specifically enumerated violations
choice_b: Having demonstrated incompetency to act as a real estate licensee in a manner that safeguards the interests of the public
choice_c: Only a criminal conviction can trigger discipline; incompetence alone is never sufficient
choice_d: Incompetency is a ground for discipline only during a licensee's first year of licensure
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(25) provides a broader, catch-all-style ground for discipline: demonstrated incompetency to act as a real estate licensee in a manner that safeguards the interests of the public -- allowing GREC to act even when a licensee's conduct does not fit neatly into one of the other, more specific enumerated grounds.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(27), how many years must a licensee keep a true and correct copy of all sales contracts and closing statements?
choice_d: There is no specific statutory retention period for sales contracts or closing statements
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(27) makes it an unfair trade practice to fail to keep, for a period of 3 years, a true and correct copy of all sales contracts and closing statements -- a specific statutory retention period, not merely a general best-practices recommendation.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: A licensee alters a closing date on a signed sales contract after the fact, without the parties' knowledge, to make a transaction appear to have closed on time. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(28), what has occurred?
choice_a: Nothing improper, as long as the change does not affect the sale price
choice_b: A violation only if the alteration is later discovered by a party to the transaction
choice_c: A violation only if the licensee is also charged criminally for forgery
choice_d: Falsification of a portion of a contract or other document involved in a real estate transaction -- an enumerated unfair trade practice
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(28) makes it an unfair trade practice for a licensee to be or become a party to any falsification of any portion of a contract or other document involved in a real estate transaction -- the violation exists independent of criminal forgery charges or later discovery.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: One licensee pressures a client into demanding that a cooperating licensee reduce their commission, without that cooperating licensee's prior written consent. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(35), what has occurred?
choice_a: Inducing a person to alter, modify, or change another licensee's fee or commission without that licensee's prior written consent -- an enumerated unfair trade practice
choice_b: Nothing improper -- commission amounts are entirely unregulated once a transaction is underway
choice_c: A violation only if the cooperating licensee later sues in civil court for the lost commission
choice_d: A violation only between licensees at the same firm, not licensees at different firms
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(35) enumerates, as an unfair trade practice, inducing any person to alter, modify, or change another licensee's fee or commission for real estate brokerage services without that licensee's prior written consent -- applicable regardless of whether the two licensees share a firm.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: A licensee holding only a Community Association Manager (CAM) license personally negotiates the sale of a member's condominium unit, an act reserved by Chapter 43-40 to brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(31), what has this CAM licensee done?
choice_a: Nothing improper, since any GREC license authorizes any real estate activity
choice_b: Attempted to perform an act reserved to a broker, associate broker, or salesperson while licensed only as a community association manager -- an enumerated unfair trade practice
choice_c: A violation only if the CAM licensee also collected a commission on the sale
choice_d: A violation only if the association's board did not know about the transaction
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(31) makes it an unfair trade practice for a CAM licensee to attempt to perform an act that Chapter 43-40 reserves only to a broker, associate broker, or salesperson -- reflecting that a CAM license does not authorize general brokerage activity, consistent with CAM being a separate, distinct license track.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: A CAM licensee sells a unit belonging to a member of the community association the CAM manages, without obtaining the association's express written consent to do so. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(32), what has occurred?
choice_a: Nothing improper, since a CAM licensee's authority over member units is unlimited by default
choice_b: A violation only if the sale price was below fair market value
choice_c: Attempting to sell, lease, or exchange a community association member's property, to which the licensee provides CAM services, without the association's express written consent -- an enumerated unfair trade practice
choice_d: A violation only if the CAM licensee is not also a licensed broker
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(32) makes it an unfair trade practice for a licensee providing CAM services to attempt to sell, lease, or exchange the property of an association member without the association's express written consent to do so.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: A community association terminates its management contract with a CAM licensee's firm. Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(33), what must be delivered to the association within 30 days of termination (or such other period the contract provides)?
choice_a: Nothing -- the firm may retain all association records and funds indefinitely once the contract ends
choice_b: Only the association's funds; records and documents may be retained by the firm as proprietary business records
choice_c: Only a final invoice for services rendered, with no obligation to return records or funds
choice_d: A complete and accurate record of all transactions and funds handled and not previously accounted for, all records/documents received from or on behalf of the association, and any funds held on the association's behalf
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-25(b)(33) requires a management-contract termination to be followed, within 30 days (or such other period the contract specifies), by delivery to the association of a complete and accurate accounting record, all association-related records/documents, and any funds held on the association's behalf -- failing to do so is an enumerated unfair trade practice.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29, is a property owner (or the owner's own employee) who manages or leases the owner's own property required to hold a Georgia real estate license to do so?
choice_a: No -- O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29(a) exempts an owner and the owner's own employees from licensure for acts performed with respect to the owner's own property
choice_b: Yes -- every act of managing or leasing real property in Georgia requires a real estate license, even by the owner personally
choice_c: No, but only if the property is residential; commercial owner-management always requires a license
choice_d: Yes, unless the owner personally holds a law degree
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29(a) exempts a property owner, and the owner's own employees, from Georgia's real estate licensing requirement when performing acts (such as management or leasing) with respect to property the owner itself holds -- since they are not acting on behalf of others for compensation in the way licensure is designed to regulate.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29, is a licensed Georgia attorney required to separately hold a real estate license to perform real-estate-related acts that are merely incidental to that attorney's law practice?
choice_a: Yes -- every attorney who touches any real estate matter must separately obtain a broker's license
choice_b: No -- attorneys acting incidentally to the practice of law are exempted from the real estate licensing requirement for that incidental activity
choice_c: No, but only if the attorney has practiced law in Georgia for at least 10 years
choice_d: Yes, unless the attorney is also a CPA
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29 exempts licensed attorneys from the real estate licensing requirement when their real-estate-related activity is merely incidental to their law practice -- reflecting that attorneys are separately regulated by the State Bar rather than needing a duplicate GREC license for such incidental work.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29, is a court-appointed fiduciary -- such as a receiver, trustee, administrator, executor, or guardian -- required to hold a real estate license to convey or manage real property under that court authority?
choice_a: Yes -- every fiduciary handling real property must first obtain a Georgia broker's license regardless of court appointment
choice_b: No, but only if the fiduciary is also a licensed attorney
choice_c: No -- such court-appointed fiduciaries acting under their court authority are exempted from Georgia's real estate licensing requirement for that fiduciary activity
choice_d: Yes, unless the estate's value exceeds $1 million
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29 exempts court-appointed fiduciaries -- receivers, trustees, administrators, executors, and guardians -- from the real estate licensing requirement when acting within their court-granted authority over real property, since they act under judicial oversight rather than as a licensed brokerage service to the public.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29's referral-agent exemption, what limitation generally applies to how many referred transactions an unlicensed referral agent may make in a year while remaining within the exemption?
choice_a: No limit at all -- an unlicensed referral agent may refer an unlimited number of transactions annually and remain exempt
choice_b: The exemption applies only to a single, one-time referral in the agent's lifetime
choice_c: The exemption has no numeric limit but requires GREC pre-approval of each individual referral
choice_d: The exemption generally limits an unlicensed referral agent to no more than 3 referred transactions per year, among other specified conditions (such as not accepting a fee directly from the referred party)
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29's referral-agent exemption generally limits an unlicensed person to no more than 3 referred transactions per year, along with other conditions (such as not accepting compensation directly from the referred party), to remain within the exemption rather than needing a real estate license.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29, may a broker employ an unlicensed assistant to help with certain tasks, and if so, what limitation applies?
choice_a: Yes -- a broker may employ an unlicensed assistant under written authorization, but the assistant's tasks are generally limited to ministerial (clerical/administrative) functions rather than activities requiring a license, such as negotiating terms
choice_b: No -- Georgia law categorically bars a broker from having any unlicensed employees whatsoever
choice_c: Yes, without any limitation on the type of tasks the unlicensed assistant may perform, including negotiating price
choice_d: Yes, but only if the unlicensed assistant is a licensed CPA
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29 permits a broker to employ an unlicensed assistant under written authorization, but the assistant's permitted role is generally limited to ministerial (clerical/administrative) tasks -- such as scheduling or preparing paperwork -- rather than activities that themselves require licensure, like negotiating a transaction's terms.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29, does the short-term-rental exemption generally apply to rentals of any length, or is it limited to rentals under a specified duration?
choice_a: It applies to rentals of any length, including multi-year leases
choice_b: The exemption generally applies only to certain short-term rentals of under 90 days, meeting other specified conditions -- not to longer-term leasing arrangements
choice_c: The exemption applies only to rentals exceeding one year
choice_d: There is no duration limitation of any kind under this exemption
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29's short-term-rental exemption generally applies to certain rentals under 90 days (subject to other specified conditions), rather than extending to longer-term residential leasing arrangements, which fall outside that narrow carve-out.

topic: License Law, Commission Discipline & Recovery Fund
question: Under O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29, do these licensing exemptions apply to a person who already holds a Georgia real estate license, or to someone using the exemption to evade the licensing requirement?
choice_a: Yes -- the exemptions apply broadly to everyone, including current licensees and anyone attempting to use them to avoid licensure
choice_b: The exemptions apply only to current licensees, not to unlicensed persons at all
choice_c: The exemptions generally do not apply to persons who already hold a real estate license or to those attempting to use an exemption to evade the licensing requirement -- they are meant for genuinely non-licensed, non-brokerage activity
choice_d: The exemptions apply automatically to any person regardless of intent or licensure status
explanation: O.C.G.A. § 43-40-29's exemptions are limited: they generally do not extend to persons who already hold a real estate license (who remain subject to license-law obligations) or to someone using an exemption as a pretext to evade the licensing requirement -- the exemptions are meant for genuinely non-brokerage activity falling outside the statute's licensing purpose.
